findings.where: Hero, the standfirst under the headline (desktop and phone): "Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience"
findings.fault: The proof beside the page's one action is a size word: a count of years. The one checkable fact, Lead Lawyer in the World Bank's PPP Group, has to share the line with it, and nothing near the button points to any named work, body or region. The first claim a visitor checks is a boast, not evidence.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff choosing a consultant against terms of reference judge by relevant work, kind of project and region, not by length of career. Mark ruled out big claims too ('one strong line, no boasts', client value 6). A '40 years' line reads as the firm voice the brand sheet §5 turns away from.

findings.where: Hero, the first screen as a whole (desktop-01, phone-01)
findings.fault: The 5-second test half passes. A reader can tell what this is and who is behind it, but not who it is for or where Mark works. No line names development banks or agencies, and none names the regions or countries of his work.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor from a development agency can't tell straight away that Mark works for clients like them and in their region. That is the first thing an advisor's visitor must be sure of before writing (first-visit trust items 2 and 6).

findings.where: Motion sketch: the principle words "precise, light, quick", the brisk easing and the heading chosen as the element entering; and the hero, where the headline, standfirst and button arrive together
findings.fault: The motion character the tile sets is brisk and text-led. The first thing to move is the headline, at 0 ms, and the button is in view at once. Nothing gives the quiet moment before the words ask, and the motion doesn't involve the mark that the v5 card calls the only picture.
findings.who_objects: Mark asked for 'calm first': one quiet picture or moment before any text asks for anything (client value 2). He also asked that the logo be built by the opening. The animation round (#9) would inherit a principle, 'quick', that works against both.

findings.where: Style tile, Type pair (desktop-02): Gelasio in the left column, Source Sans 3 across the gutter in the right column
findings.fault: The pair is split across the tile's two columns, about 500 px apart, with nothing joining the two specimens. They read as two separate items under a heading that reaches only the left one, not as one pairing seen together.
findings.who_objects: Mark, or whoever judges the direction, can't judge how the two faces sit together, and seeing that is the type pair's whole point in a tile.
